comment: The shared rules for the disk a probe stick (or IntelXe Manager's installer stick) may be written to: the facts about one disk and the codes of the reasons to refuse it ([] = may be written). Run by tools/probe-stick/test/disk-rules-test.sh through write-stick.sh --rules, and by IntelXe.Core.Tests (StickDiskVectorTests) through StickRules. bus: usb, virtual, or another bus (nvme, sata, sas, raid, sd, spaces). system: the disk holds the running system (Windows: IsBoot/IsSystem). whole: false only where a tool can be handed a partition (write-stick.sh); the Windows app lists whole disks only (windows: false). minimum: the image's size in bytes (the probe stick); maxBytes: the size above which a disk is refused unless allowLarge.
efiComment: The EFI rule for one partition: esp (an EFI system partition by its type: GPT C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B or MBR 0xEF; Windows never opens it, write-stick.sh looks inside when it can), opencore (EFI/OC/OpenCore.efi on it), bootx64 (EFI/BOOT/BOOTx64.efi on it), probe (xe-probe-stick.marker on it: a probe stick, whose BOOTx64.efi is its own GRUB). efi: the codes of what erasing it loses ([] = no EFI). A disk holds an EFI when one of its partitions gives a code; it is not refused, but erasing it needs a confirmation of its own (IntelXe Manager: a box to tick and the helpers' --erase-efi; write-stick.sh: ERASE EFI typed, or --erase-efi). Run by disk-rules-test.sh through write-stick.sh --efi-rules, and by IntelXe.Core.Tests through StickRules.HoldsEfi.
